summary: Robert Ford Campany is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He served as a professor at Indiana University from around 1989 to 2004 and held a post at Vanderbilt University around 2010.

Robert Gardner earned his BA from Harvard University (ca. 1943–1947). He worked at the Fogg Museum, taught at the University of Puget Sound (1950–1953), founded Harvard University in 1957, and served as a professor there from 1956 to 1997.

Robert Gauthiot was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 1900–1905 and became a member of the Société Asiatique in 1909.

Robert Göbl was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna (1947–1950), where he later held an academic post from around 1955 to 1989.

Robert H. Brower studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan. A Japanologist, he taught at Minnesota (1951–1954) and Stanford (1954–1966), directed the Inter-University Center (1963–1964), and chaired Michigan's Department of Far Eastern Languages and Literatures (1966–1988).

Robert H. Sharf studied at Toronto, Kyoto, and Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and Kenneth J. DeWoskin. A scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology, he taught at McMaster and Michigan, becoming a professor at UC Berkeley around 2004.
Robert Hinde studied at St John's College (~1941–1947) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1948–1950). He held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1950 to 1989.
Robert Hyde Colebrooke worked in history and archaeology. He was a member of The Asiatic Society (1785–1802) and served as Surveyor General at the Survey of India from 1794 to 1808.

Robert J. Miller worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from around 1956 to 1989 and also held a professorship at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Robert Kritzer, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, completed his PhD at UC Berkeley in 1995 under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He served as an associate professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).
Robert Kyd studied at the University of Edinburgh and founded the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden in 1787.
Robert L. Brown was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He was a curator of South and Southeast Asian art at LACMA (~1981–2014) and a professor at UCLA (~1986–2014).

Robert Lenz studied at Tartu and under Franz Bopp at Berlin. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he taught at Tallinn Cathedral School (~1828–1830) and was a professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University (~1835–1836).

Robert M. Gimello earned his PhD at Columbia University (~1969–1976). A scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, he held posts at the University of Arizona (~1981–2020) and Harvard University (~2000–2006).

Robert Maclagan studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering. A scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology, he served as Principal of IIT Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

Robert Magliola completed his PhD at Princeton University (~1966–1970). A scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Purdue, Tamkang, Assumption, and National Taiwan universities, and Columbia University (2002–2011).

Robert Mayer is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bristol and Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen, and joined Oxford's Oriental Studies faculty in 2002.

Robert Needham Cust was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He was educated at Eton, Trinity College Cambridge, East India Company College, and Fort William College, and served in the Bengal Civil Service from around 1843 to 1867.

Robert P. Goldman studied at Columbia and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, S. D. Joshi, and Shrinivasa Shastri. An Indologist, he became a professor at the University of California, Berkeley, beginning around 1971.

Robert S. Ellwood studied at the University of Colorado, Yale, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. A scholar of religious studies and Japanology, he served on the faculty at the University of Southern California (~1967–1997).
